chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashem quoted on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abil Salt al-Harawi that he had heard Ar-Ridha (peace be upon him) say:

By God! All of us will be killed and become a martyr. He was asked, 'O son of the Prophet of God! Who will murder you?' He replied, 'The most wicked creature of God in my time will kill me using poison. Then he will bury me in a very tight house in a strange town. Know that whoever visits me in my loneliness, God the Highest will record for him the reward of one-hundred thousand martyrs, one-hundred thousand honest ones, one-hundred thousand obligatory and 'Umra pilgrimages, and one-hundred thousands fighters in the way of God. He will also be resurrected among us (the 12 Imams). He will be established in high ranks in Heaven as our friend.'

key_terms.شَرُّ خَلْقِ اللَّهِ: the most wicked creature of God

ai.seo_question: Who will kill Imam Ar-Ridha and what is the reward for visiting him in his ghurba?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida*, Imam al-Rida (a.s.) identifies his assassin as the 'worst of creation' of his era, a reference widely understood by Shia scholars as the Caliph al-Ma'mun, emphasizing the political nature of his martyrdom. The concept of 'ghurba' (strangeness/loneliness) here signifies not just physical exile in Tus, but the spiritual isolation of the Imamate amidst the Abbasid court, making the visitation (ziyara) an act of profound loyalty. This immense reward structure underscores the theological importance of the Imam's physical presence and shrine as a locus of divine grace and intercession.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 66-9 Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashem quoted on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abil Salt al-Harawi that he had heard Ar-Ridha’ (a.s.) say, “By God! All of us will be killed and become a martyr.”

He was asked, “O son of the Prophet of God (Ar-Ridha’ (a.s.)! Who will murder you?” He replied, “The most wicked creature of God in my time (Al-Ma’mun) will kill me using poison. Then he will bury me in a very tight house in a strange town. Know that whoever visits me in my loneliness, God the Highest will record for him the reward of one-hundred thousand martyrs, one-hundred thousand honest ones, one-hundred thousand obligatory and ‘Umra (a.s.upererogatory) pilgrimages, and one-hundred thousands fighters in the way of God. He will also be resurrected among us (the 12 Imams (a.s.)). He will be established in high ranks in Heaven as our friend.”
